claim.summary: src/click/parser.py is Click's internal, optparse-derived parser. _OptionParser holds short/long option tables and positional _Argument specs. parse_args first scans options (_process_args_for_options) and then assigns positionals via _unpack_args. It returns (opts dict, leftover args, order list of Parameter objects). Core's Command.make_parser builds it and Option/Argument.add_to_parser register params. Old public names (OptionParser, Option, Argument, split_opt, normalize_opt, ParsingState, split_arg_string) are served by a module __getattr__ that emits DeprecationWarning.

interfaces.name: _OptionParser
interfaces.behavior: Internal parser. __init__(ctx=None) sets allow_interspersed_args=True and ignore_unknown_options=False, then copies both from ctx if given. Maintains _short_opt, _long_opt dicts, _opt_prefixes={'-','--'}, _args list. Docstring marks it deprecated 8.2, removal in 9.0.
edge_cases: ctx None is allowed: no token normalization, no resilient parsing

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.add_option
interfaces.behavior: Normalizes each opt string via _normalize_opt (ctx.token_normalize_func), builds an _Option, adds its prefixes to _opt_prefixes, and registers short opts in _short_opt and long opts in _long_opt. dest is not inferred. Actions: store, store_const, append, append_const, count (default store).
edge_cases: Option string with no prefix (starts with alnum) raises ValueError from _Option
Later registration of the same opt string overwrites the earlier one
Custom prefixes such as + or ! get added to _opt_prefixes

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.add_argument
interfaces.behavior: Appends an _Argument(obj, dest, nargs) to _args. Order of calls determines positional order.
edge_cases: nargs=-1 means consume the remainder; two nargs<0 args later raise TypeError in _unpack_args

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.parse_args
interfaces.behavior: Creates _ParsingState(args), runs _process_args_for_options then _process_args_for_args, and returns (state.opts, state.largs, state.order). Mutates the passed list (rargs is popped).
edge_cases: UsageError is swallowed when ctx is not None and ctx.resilient_parsing is True, returning the partial state
Without ctx, UsageError always propagates

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_args_for_options
interfaces.behavior: Loop popping from rargs. '--' stops option processing and is consumed (dropped). An arg whose first char is in _opt_prefixes and len>1 goes to _process_opts. Otherwise, with allow_interspersed_args it is appended to largs, else it is pushed back onto rargs and parsing stops.
edge_cases: A lone '-' is treated as a positional
Without interspersed args, the first non-option stops option parsing

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_args_for_args
interfaces.behavior: Calls _unpack_args on largs+rargs using each arg's nargs, calls each _Argument.process with its slice, then sets largs to the leftovers and rargs to [].
edge_cases: Surplus values stay in largs, which is the returned leftover list
Missing values become UNSET

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_opts
interfaces.behavior: Splits arg on the first '=' into long_opt and explicit_value, normalizes, and tries _match_long_opt. On NoSuchOption: if arg[:2] is not a known prefix (for example '-abc'), falls back to _match_short_opt. Otherwise, re-raises unless ignore_unknown_options, in which case the whole arg goes to largs.
edge_cases: '-foo' can match a registered long option with a single dash
Short-option clusters are only tried for single-char prefixes

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._match_long_opt
interfaces.behavior: Looks up opt in _long_opt. If the option takes a value, an explicit '=value' is inserted at the front of rargs and then read by _get_value_from_state. Otherwise the value is UNSET, then option.process is called.
edge_cases: Unknown opt raises NoSuchOption with possibilities=_long_opt for suggestions
A flag given '=value' raises BadOptionUsage

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._match_short_opt
interfaces.behavior: Iterates over the characters of a cluster like -abc. Each character is normalized and looked up in _short_opt. A value-taking option consumes the remainder of the cluster as its value (pushed onto rargs) and stops.
edge_cases: With ignore_unknown_options, unknown characters are collected and re-appended to largs as prefix+chars
Otherwise unknown raises NoSuchOption

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._get_value_from_state
interfaces.behavior: Gets the option value from rargs. If fewer than nargs remain: returns FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE when option.obj._flag_needs_value, else raises. For nargs==1 the next token is used, except that with _flag_needs_value a following token that looks like an option gives FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE. For nargs>1 returns a tuple and consumes nargs items.
edge_cases: Value tokens that start with a prefix are consumed as values for ordinary options

interfaces.name: _Option
interfaces.behavior: Holds the parsed option spec: _short_opts (prefix len 1 and name len 1), _long_opts (everything else), prefixes, dest, action (default 'store'), nargs, const, obj. takes_value is true for store and append. process(value, state) applies the action to state.opts and appends obj to state.order.
edge_cases: Unknown action raises ValueError('unknown action ...') at process time, not at construction
count starts from 0 and increments
append and append_const use setdefault lists

interfaces.name: _Option.process
interfaces.behavior: store sets opts[dest]=value; store_const sets const; append and append_const append to a list; count increments. Always appends obj to state.order, so repeated options are recorded repeatedly.
edge_cases: Unknown action raises ValueError

interfaces.name: _Argument.process
interfaces.behavior: For nargs>1: if all items are UNSET the value becomes UNSET, if only some are it raises BadArgumentUsage. An empty tuple becomes UNSET. Stores into state.opts[dest] and appends obj to state.order.
edge_cases: nargs=-1 with no values gives UNSET (not an empty tuple)

interfaces.name: _ParsingState
interfaces.behavior: Holds mutable parse state: opts dict, largs (leftovers/positionals), rargs (remaining), order list.

interfaces.name: _unpack_args
interfaces.behavior: Distributes args across the nargs_spec. nargs==1 gives a str, nargs>1 gives a tuple, nargs<0 is a wildcard that takes the remainder. Specs after the wildcard are filled from the end, then reversed. Returns (tuple of values, leftover list). Missing values are UNSET.
edge_cases: Only one wildcard is allowed
Without a wildcard, excess args are returned as leftovers

interfaces.name: _split_opt
interfaces.behavior: Returns (prefix, rest). If the first char is alphanumeric the prefix is ''. If the first two chars are equal ('--') the prefix is two chars. Otherwise the prefix is one char.
edge_cases: An empty string gives ('', '')

interfaces.name: _normalize_opt
interfaces.behavior: Returns opt unchanged if ctx is None or has no token_normalize_func. Otherwise splits off the prefix and applies the function to the name only.

interfaces.name: __getattr__
interfaces.behavior: Module-level deprecation shim. Names OptionParser, Argument, Option, split_opt, normalize_opt, ParsingState return globals()['_<name>'] with a DeprecationWarning (stacklevel 2). split_arg_string is re-imported from shell_completion with a warning. Anything else raises AttributeError.
edge_cases: Other unknown names raise AttributeError(name)

claim.error_conventions: Parse problems raise click.exceptions UsageError subclasses. NoSuchOption is for an unknown option (with a possibilities list for suggestions). BadOptionUsage(option_name, msg) covers a missing value, a value given to a flag, or a wrong nargs count. BadArgumentUsage covers a partially filled multi-value positional. Programmer errors use ValueError (invalid option prefix or unknown action) and TypeError (two nargs<0). Messages are gettext-wrapped (`_` and `ngettext`) and use repr-quoted names, e.g. "Option {name!r} requires an argument." / "Option {name!r} requires {nargs} arguments." / "Option {name!r} does not take a value." / "Argument {name!r} takes {nargs} values.". The ValueError and TypeError messages: "Invalid start character for option ({option})" is translated, "Cannot have two nargs < 0" is not.

examples.description: Parser defaults to only - and -- as prefixes
Custom option prefixes are collected when options are added
examples.code:
ctx = click.Context(click.Command("test"))
parser = _OptionParser(ctx)
click.Option("+p", is_flag=True).add_to_parser(parser, ctx)
click.Option("!e", is_flag=True).add_to_parser(parser, ctx)
assert parser._opt_prefixes == {"-", "--", "+", "!"}

parser = _OptionParser(ctx)
# ... params add themselves via param.add_to_parser(parser, ctx)

tests.how_it_asserts: Plain pytest asserts. It checks private state (_opt_prefixes) directly on _OptionParser, both default and after Option.add_to_parser with custom prefixes '+' and '!'. It also has a parametrized test of shell_completion.split_arg_string. There are no direct tests of the parse_args error paths. Those are covered indirectly by the CliRunner-based tests for options and arguments elsewhere (not read).

extension_points.name: Command.make_parser
extension_points.what_could_attach: Override in a Command subclass to return a customized _OptionParser (a subclass with different matching rules) or to pre-register extra options.

extension_points.name: Parameter.add_to_parser (Option/Argument)
extension_points.what_could_attach: Custom Option/Argument subclasses decide how they register with the parser (action, nargs, const, dest).

extension_points.name: Context.token_normalize_func via _normalize_opt
extension_points.what_could_attach: Supplying token_normalize_func on the Context changes how option names are matched (case-insensitive or alias handling).

extension_points.name: _Option.process action dispatch
extension_points.what_could_attach: A new action (for example 'extend') could be added to the if/elif chain and to takes_value.

extension_points.name: _OptionParser.allow_interspersed_args / ignore_unknown_options
extension_points.what_could_attach: Context flags that tune parsing. Plugins can set them via Context settings.

gaps.description: No abbreviation or prefix matching of long options (such as --verb for --verbose)
gaps.why_plausible: _match_long_opt does an exact dict lookup. NoSuchOption already gets the possibilities list, so a unique-prefix lookup would fit in the same place.

gaps.description: No 'extend' action and no per-option duplicate-use detection or error
gaps.why_plausible: The actions are a fixed set. Repeated store options silently overwrite, though state.order already records repeats.

gaps.description: No explicit '=' value support for short options (-o=val keeps '=' as part of the value)
gaps.why_plausible: Short-cluster handling just pushes the remainder of the cluster as the value.

gaps.description: Duplicate or conflicting option registration is not detected
gaps.why_plausible: add_option silently overwrites existing entries in the dict.

limitations: Module and class are internal and deprecated. _OptionParser is marked deprecated since 8.2 and slated for removal in 9.0, and the module docstring plans to remove more.
Only the actions store, store_const, append, append_const and count exist, and they are plain strings validated lazily.
Only one nargs=-1 positional is supported.
The parser does no type conversion, defaults or validation. Those live in core.
Argument parsing is two-phase: all options are processed before positional assignment, so positional nargs cannot influence option parsing.
Tests for this module are minimal; direct unit coverage of parsing behavior is thin.
